summary: Round 3, verify only, docs-only. M4.8-R2a IS FIXED -- but not in the bytes I was issued. The packet bound me to b9600148 (tree 8edda6a2), in which the inverted sentence 'M4.1's row records the missing-sort mutation killed about 1 run in 6 at three streams' still stood verbatim three clauses after the clause correcting it, contradicting it inside one row; I found it independently and confirmed it in the index with `git show :`. The tree was then edited WHILE THIS REVIEW WAS RUNNING (review.md rule 12b): the duplicate is deleted at the current hash and an unrelated new M4.8b clause appeared, so I re-judged against the live bytes. At those bytes the surviving statement matches backlog-done.md:110 exactly ('at three streams a broken sort still produced the asserted order about 1 run in 6' -> killed ~5 in 6), so R2a is closed. R2b is closed: the summary now states the defect rather than a prohibition, 'THE MANDATED KEY' matches SPEC.md:269's normative grammar, and both copies now say the row does not choose. R2c's mechanism is verified -- cost.md R15 is the ~1 LIST/s ceiling (cost.md:73), SPEC.md:299-302 does put recovery behind it at 300-node fan-out, and sdd.md rule 8 does say a wrong spec is amended -- but the ASYMMETRY the fix states is not supported (F3 below). R2d is fixed in the notes copy and left standing in backlog.md (F1). Four minors, none blocking: two are the recurring 'claim the record does not support', one is the recurring one-copy-fixed, and one is the process breach that moved the bytes under the review.

findings.summary: R2d WAS FIXED IN ONE COPY AND ITS DUPLICATE STILL SAYS THE OPPOSITE -- the exact failure this commit's own banner names. backlog-notes.md:169 now reads 'THE SOURCE TEXT NOW LIVES IN THE SUB-ROWS rather than here'. backlog.md:117, which links to that anchor and is untouched by this diff, still reads 'this row is the source text and is not itself implemented. It carries three separable pieces'. Neither row carries the source text any more -- M4.8a-c do -- so the backlog.md sentence is false on its own terms and contradicts the notes row it points at, in the two tables that decide what gets built. This is the same shape as round 1's F2 (notes said `todo`, backlog said `split`), reintroduced by the fix for R2d, and the M4.8 banner three lines away states the rule it breaks: 'BOTH COPIES OF A SPLIT MUST SAY SO'. Rated minor rather than major only because the consequence is a wasted lookup, not a wrong build: unlike F2, nothing here makes M4.8 look implementable -- both copies carry the SPLIT banner and the state `split`.
findings.failure_scenario: backlog.md is the file every session loads whole (check-session-load.sh bounds it for that reason), so 'this row is the source text' is the copy most readers see. A later auditor re-checking the split -- exactly the audit the notes row was rewritten to make repeatable -- reads backlog.md, believes the pre-split wording is in the M4.8 row, opens it, finds a two-line summary, and has to work out which of two same-commit statements binds before it can start. The clause-coverage check the notes row exists to enable is the thing that gets skipped.

findings.summary: 'ROUND-1 REVIEW VERIFIED CLAUSE BY CLAUSE' IS ATTRIBUTED TO THE WRONG ROUND, IN THE SENTENCE WHOSE ONLY JOB IS TO MAKE THE CHECK AUDITABLE. The round-1 production verdict (.harness/review/6ff441b7...reviewer.json) contains no clause-coverage check at all -- its three findings are the ckpt/logPrefix collision, the todo-vs-split disagreement, and the falsified round-count universal, and its summary says so. The clause-by-clause check is in the ROUND-2 verdict (dd5da0a2...reviewer.json, finding M4.8-R2d): 'I checked every clause of the deleted M4.8 text against the three sub-rows and none was lost (record fields to M4.8a, K/T plus key grammar plus the ADR-0022 ordering argument to M4.8b, zero-LIST discovery plus candidates plus the >5,000 workload to M4.8c, the not-the-offset-index rationale and the ~38 KiB figure to M4.8a)'. The mapping the row records is right; the round it credits is not. Fixing it is one word ('Round-2').
findings.failure_scenario: The row is the pointer a future auditor follows, and .harness/review is gitignored and keyed by diff hash, so 'round 1' is the only handle it gives. An auditor re-splitting or re-scoping M4.8a-c looks up the round-1 verdict, finds three findings about a prefix collision and none about clause coverage, and concludes either that the check never happened or that the row is unreliable -- which is the state the row was rewritten to prevent. It is also this task's recurring defect (a claim the record does not support) landing in the one sentence that claims to make the record checkable.

findings.summary: THE COST ASYMMETRY THE R2C FIX STATES IS NOT SUPPORTED, AND IT IS ON THIS PROJECT'S ONE AXIS. The row now says '(a) A SUFFIX FILTER ... leaves chainEnd and applyChain LISTing a prefix whose key count grows with every checkpoint ... so recovery's LIST count grows WITH UPTIME ... (b) A KEY OUTSIDE THE LISTED PREFIX has no such growth'. (b) has essentially the same growth. The prefix ChainReplay lists is CommitLog.logPrefix() = <prefix>/ctl/log/0/<epoch:016x>/ (CommitLog.java:114-116), and chainEnd pages it 1,000 keys at a time (ChainReplay.java:97-105) over the DELTA keys, one per commit, which nothing deletes before M7 either. So LIST pages already grow with uptime under both remedies; checkpoints are written once per K deltas, so (a) adds a factor of at most 1 + 1/K (bounded by 2 even when T dominates), not a new dimension. The tree already says so twice: SPEC.md:265-267 attributes the uptime growth to paging the ckpt/ prefix for DISCOVERY, and M4.9's own note in this same file (backlog-notes.md:173) records the measured growth of recovery's LISTs per ancestor chain and owns bounding it. Note this framing originated in my own round-2 R2c, which said the LIST count grows with uptime under (a) and was silent about (b) -- the fix turned an incomplete statement into a false contrast. The row's actual prescription (do not choose; the takeover test carries a request-count dimension) is right and survives the correction; only the differential is wrong. Same clause, an off-by-one nit not worth its own finding: M4.8c is one row down, not 'two rows down'.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.8b's implementer reads the two remedies as differing in KIND on cost, rejects the suffix filter to avoid a cost.md R15 breach, and amends the M4 SPEC's normative key grammar (sdd.md rule 8, a wire-format-adjacent change) to buy a factor of 1/K on a LIST that still grows with uptime from the delta keys. The R15 exposure is unchanged either way and is M4.9's to remove, so the SPEC amendment is paid for with a false cost argument -- and because the same sentence now sits in backlog.md's summary row ('The two remedies differ in cost and this row does not choose'), the next reader inherits the differential without the arithmetic.

findings.summary: THE ARGUED ROUND-CAP ENTRY OPENS WITH A UNIVERSAL ITS OWN NEXT SENTENCES REFUTE. 'Every finding across both rounds was a row PRESCRIBING A TEST THAT WOULD NOT DISCRIMINATE' is false against .harness: round 1's F2 (notes row says `todo` while backlog.md says `split`) and F3 (a round-count universal the review record falsifies) prescribe no test, and round 2's R2a (the inverted M4.1 measurement), R2b (two copies of one constraint disagreeing) and R2d (the row claiming to be source text after the source text was deleted) prescribe none either -- roughly half the findings were prose-consistency findings. The entry itself then says 'TWO CLAIMS OF MINE WERE FALSE AND ARE CORRECTED IN PLACE' and names F3's and R2a's subjects, i.e. two findings that were not test prescriptions. The other two legs of the argument are sound and sufficient on their own -- every fix was a single clause in one row, and the checkpoint-contents gap was visible only across a, b and c at once -- and I accept the exception on those. The mechanics are correct: `rounds:M4.8` is the first field, a reason follows, and the line is ADDED in a staged baselines/review.txt (review.md rule two-round-cap). The remedy is one word: 'Every' -> 'Every test-prescription finding', or 'Most'.
findings.failure_scenario: baselines/review.txt is read by sessions that have only .harness, and its worth is that its entries are checkable -- the M4.43 entry two lines up says exactly that about itself. A later session mining this file for why the cap keeps firing counts M4.8 as evidence that decomposition rows fail only on test prescriptions, and does not learn the thing this task actually demonstrates twice: that the recurring defect in a docs commit is a claim the record does not support and one copy of a fact fixed while its duplicate stands. That is the same class of overstatement round 1 majored as F3, in the file that exists to stop it recurring.

findings.summary: THE STAGED BYTES WERE EDITED WHILE THIS REVIEW WAS RUNNING (review.md rule 12b). The packet I was issued is bound to staged sha256 b9600148 / tree 8edda6a2; the index now hashes to 7aa7aa15 / tree f280bc30. Two edits landed mid-round: the inverted duplicate at backlog-notes.md:321 was deleted (closing M4.8-R2a, which I had already confirmed present with `git show :` at the packet bytes), and backlog-notes.md:325 gained a new clause requiring the two-trigger keys to be 'DISTINCT AND STRICTLY INCREASING', which appeared in no packet issued to this role. I judged that clause on its merits rather than passing bytes unread -- it is sound, and it closes the non-monotone-seq mutation that the formatter-scoped grammar assertion cannot see -- and this verdict is deliberately bound to the CURRENT hash so it certifies bytes I actually read.
findings.failure_scenario: A verdict is bound to a hash, and the next round's packet diffs against the tree stored with the last verdict. An edit made after the packet is generated and before the verdict is recorded therefore lands inside the reviewed hash while having been shown to nobody, and it is invisible in the next round's delta because that delta starts from the tree this verdict records. Had I recorded without re-reading, the new M4.8b clause would carry a production verdict no reviewer was ever shown -- and if the tree moves again before commit, check-reviewed.sh refuses and the round is spent for nothing, which is the cost review.md rule 12b was written from.
